Flagship · Defensathon 2026 · Next: ApexNav at SAIF

NavPod

A navigation pod that keeps a fixed-wing UAV flying when GPS is jammed or gone.

Problem
Electronic warfare jams GPS and datalinks. A small UAV that loses both loses its position and its mission.
Approach
Preload a satellite baseline map. Onboard cameras run visual SLAM and match live terrain to that map, so the aircraft knows where it is with no GNSS at all.
My role
UAV systems engineer. Built the MATLAB/Simulink model from scratch: 12-state 6-DOF BWB dynamics with elevon mixing, a 15-state EKF and L1 guidance. Designed the pod in SolidWorks, ran CFD on it, and owned the mass budget.
Result
2nd place nationally at Defensathon 2026, university track, 15,000 SAR. Featured in Saudi News coverage.
Next
Upgrading into ApexNav, the next model, heading to SAIF: terrain navigation without GPS, AI-aided INS drift correction and a hardware-in-the-loop sim.

NavPod · engineering file
bwb_eom.m · from my 6-DOF model
%% BWB elevon mixing
de = 0.5*(dL + dR);    % elevator (symmetric)
da = 0.5*(dL - dR);    % aileron  (differential)

%% Translational EOM  (Newton in rotating body frame)
u_dot = Fx/p.m + rb*v - qb*w;
v_dot = Fy/p.m + pb*w - rb*u;
w_dot = Fz/p.m + qb*u - pb*v;

%% Rotational EOM  (Stevens & Lewis c1 to c8)
p_dot = (p.c1*rb + p.c2*pb)*qb + p.c3*L_aero + p.c4*N_aero;
q_dot =  p.c5*pb*rb - p.c6*(pb^2 - rb^2) + M_aero/p.Iyy;
r_dot = (p.c7*pb - p.c2*rb)*qb + p.c4*L_aero + p.c8*N_aero;

GPS-denied navigation, live

A survey flight over open terrain. Cut the GPS and watch two estimates: raw inertial navigation drifting away, and NavPod pulling itself back each time its camera matches a known terrain feature.

Illustrative model: accelerometer bias drives quadratic INS drift; a landmark inside the camera footprint triggers a position fix, and a learned bias correction slows drift between fixes. Units scaled for display.

Gas dynamics · ME 1446 · Jun 2026

PSP shock mapping

A full test campaign to map the surface pressure under an oblique shock on a supersonic wedge, using pressure-sensitive paint that turns pressure into light.

Problem
Pressure taps give a few points. A shock footprint is sharp, so you need the whole surface field, not samples.
Approach
Paint the wedge with a luminescent coating that oxygen dims. Image it wind-on and wind-off, then convert the ratio to pressure with an in-situ Stern-Volmer fit.
My role
Sole author. Designed the 5-run test matrix (M 2 to 3, θ 10° to 20°), chose binary paint to beat temperature drift, wrote the data-reduction pipeline and the uncertainty budget.
Result
Wedge chosen because theory gives exact ground truth: β ≈ 45° and a 2.19× pressure jump at the design point. The campaign doubles as a CFD validation case.
